items.title: Wilson "Willie T" Turbinton Interview, 1990-09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Do you have any special, one night that stands out in your mind as very special from the workshop? What is it, Rene?

ctx.x: Well, I think Earl is always gravitated towards sharing the experience of trying to inform people on another level. I mean, Earl would go and play in the prisons. I mean, stuff that a lot of people would shy off from. But you've got to understand that George Davis comes from a serious educational background. And one of the greatest experiences that I've had and the things that I've learned was from my experience of playing with George. I mean, George played with the Juilliard. I mean, he is a much greater…
Do you have any special, one night that stands out in your mind as very special from the workshop? What is it, Rene?

The one night that I remember more than anything is the night that Ray Charles came to the workshop. I mean, we were playing, they had three levels to the workshop. And sometimes there was like a roof that we would go up and just stand up and when we would take our breaks. And when we came down, Ray Charles was in the audience. And for me, I was such a fan of Ray Charles, just to be able to play and for him to be there and stay as long as he did. It was just such a charge for me. And then to have an opportunity…
